# AI Credit Intelligence Workbench backend

FastAPI backend for the internal credit-intelligence workbench. PostgreSQL is
the business source of truth. Kafka transports durable events, Redis provides
temporary cache/live fan-out, and MinIO stores binary artifacts. AI output is
advisory and cannot create a loan decision.

## Windows setup

Prerequisites: Python 3.12, PowerShell, Docker Desktop, and the infrastructure
stack configured under `../infra`.

```powershell
cd D:\dushdask\backend
Copy-Item .env.example .env.local
# Replace placeholders in .env.local with values generated by infra.
.\scripts\install.ps1
.\scripts\run.ps1
```

The application deliberately reads `.env.local`, not `.env`. Never commit the
local file. Infrastructure contract values keep their exact names. A process
running on Windows uses `localhost` endpoints; a container uses internal names
such as `postgres`, `kafka`, `redis`, `minio`, and `keycloak`.

Open:

- API documentation: `http://localhost:8000/docs`
- OpenAPI: `http://localhost:8000/openapi.json`
- Liveness: `http://localhost:8000/health/live`
- Readiness: `http://localhost:8000/health/ready`

## Synthetic multi-agent design runtime

When `APP_ENV` is not `production` and `LLM_PROVIDER=mock`, authenticated
employees with `loan:analyze` can exercise the real Document, Credit,
Legal/Compliance, evaluator, validator, and synthesizer code over fictional
in-memory scenarios:

```http
GET  /api/v1/agent-simulations/scenarios
POST /api/v1/agent-simulations/scenarios/READY/runs
POST /api/v1/agent-simulations/scenarios/INCOMPLETE/runs
```

Example body:

```json
{
  "objective": "Đánh giá khả năng trả nợ trên dữ liệu mô phỏng"
}
```

Every response is labelled `MOCK`, includes numbered inline mock sources and a
human-decision notice, and never writes a loan decision. Report Writer runs only
after both the expert evaluator and evidence validator pass; failed runs remain
`INCOMPLETE` and have no synthesized report. The normal conversation endpoint
also persists a parented `ASSISTANT` message in non-production mock mode, but
requires `loan:analyze` plus the persistent customer/loan assignment for expert
routes. Synthetic run IDs remain metadata and are not persisted as real
`ai.analysis_case` rows.

Selected chat attachments are authorization-checked and forwarded to the route,
but the current mock scenario does not read their bytes. The fixed infrastructure
schema has no message-attachment relation, so the exact selection is not
persisted across message reloads; no new `document_link.entity_type` is invented.

Readiness returns HTTP 503 until the PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, MinIO, and
Keycloak adapters are wired and healthy. OCR/LLM may report `mock`.

## Quality checks

```powershell
.\scripts\test.ps1
.\scripts\lint.ps1
```

Run integration tests only when infrastructure is available:

```powershell
.\scripts\test.ps1 -Integration
```

## Docker

Build from this directory without passing secrets as build arguments:

```powershell
docker build -t bank-ai-backend:local .
docker run --rm --env-file .env.local -p 8000:8000 bank-ai-backend:local
```

The image uses Python 3.12 and a non-root UID/GID `10001`.

## Process identities

Set `APP_PROCESS_TYPE=api`, `worker`, or `publisher`. Production API/publisher
processes require the `bank_app` database role; workers require `bank_worker`.
Every worker must receive its own Kafka identity. MinIO credentials are only
provided to processes that actually instantiate a storage adapter.
